name: Jawbox
label: Dischord
lede: The band that handed Atlantic a list of demands nobody expected them to meet, got every one, and ended up with a song on Beavis and Butt-Head and hate mail from home.

eras.title: A sink, a sewer, a television
eras.text: J. Robbins had been playing bass in Government Issue; now he wanted his own band, on guitar and singing. With Kim Coletta on bass and Adam Wade on drums, Jawbox came up fast in a D.C. scene that was trading hardcore speed for something knottier.

years.h: Jawbox takes its name from Brewer's Dictionary
years.p: J. Robbins, Kim Coletta and Adam Wade pull the name Jawbox from Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable, where a jawbox is a sink, a sewer, or slang for the television.

Jawbox play their first gig on a bill with Fugazi and [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. A self-titled demo EP circulates the same year, and the Jawbox song Bullet Park lands on a Maximumrocknroll compilation.

years.h: Tools & Chrome: Jawbox's debut single, DeSoto's first release
years.p: Jawbox's debut single comes out as a joint release by Dischord and DeSoto, the label run by Kim Coletta that will issue Jawbox's vinyl from then on.

eras.title: Two guitars, and a chair at the drum kit
eras.text: Jawbox's Dischord years were short and loud. Bill Barbot joined as second guitarist, Chicago engineer Iain Burgess gave them a heavier sound on Novelty, and by the end of 1992 drummer Adam Wade was gone.

years.p: Produced by [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] for under $2,000. Grip is the one song from Grippe Jawbox kept playing.
years.xp: J. Robbins later said you can hear exactly which records they were listening to on Grippe.

years.p: Bill Barbot, drummer Adam Wade's friend and roommate, joins on guitar and vocals around the Grippe release. 1991 also brings a split single with [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]] and a tour with [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]].
Jawbox's Tongues single comes out on Dischord in early 1992, between the albums Grippe and Novelty.

q: Jawbox sold like 40,000. The next step up really is Minor Threat and Fugazi.
years.p: Recorded in five days in Chicago with [[Iain Burgess|1572ff4f-9714-4d7e-804a-49b86a74a855]], engineer for [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]], who slept on J. Robbins' couch. Robbins said the sound really expanded with Bill Barbot in the band.
years.xp: Novelty and Grippe made Jawbox one of Dischord's bigger sellers. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], sizing up the catalog, put them just below the label's two biggest bands, [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].

years.h: Adam Wade quits Jawbox; [[Zach Barocas|0c8ab49f-f5d0-46b5-bee5-5aa496a70ece]] takes the drums
years.p: Right after the Novelty tour, drummer Adam Wade leaves Jawbox and soon joins [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. Zach Barocas, a friend already living in the band's building, replaces him.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Adam Wade had grown frustrated with what was going on inside Jawbox before and during the Novelty tour: J. Robbins and [[Kim Coletta|f220e94d-883b-46ce-a459-9463cce7f55d]] had ended their relationship, Coletta and [[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]] had become a couple, and Robbins' behavior turned erratic. Wade left as soon as the tour was over.

Zach Barocas settled the line-up. Robbins said his arrival really changed the band.

eras.title: Impossible demands, all accepted
eras.text: Grunge had every major label shopping in punk basements, and Jawbox had offers from Epic, Mercury and Atlantic. They signed with Atlantic, left Dischord, and kept a surprising amount of control, which didn't stop the D.C. scene from treating it as a betrayal.

years.p: Jawbox's last single for Dischord, two songs released before the band signed to Atlantic and made For Your Own Special Sweetheart.

years.big: They asked for everything. Atlantic said yes.
q: We would be stupid not to do it.
years.p: Jawbox sent Atlantic what they called a list of impossible demands: self-management, full creative control, vinyl on DeSoto. Atlantic agreed to all of it.
years.xp:
The list also covered the recording budget, merchandising and European licensing. Jawbox turned down a big advance and tour support, and asked only for studio money and enough to settle old bills. [[Mike Gitter|942763ba-3882-48b4-b0a4-513f53849530]], who knew them from the Boston hardcore scene, was their A&R man at Atlantic.

The D.C. scene took it badly. One letter-writer, the band later recalled, said he hoped they died in a fiery van accident. Drummer Zach Barocas later said the deal kept Jawbox together: he had already quit and applied to the University of Maryland.

years.h: For Your Own Special Sweetheart · Atlantic / DeSoto
years.p: Jawbox's Atlantic debut, produced by [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]] of early [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] records, took seven weeks to record against the usual seven days. It peaks at No. 28 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and, per Wikipedia, sells roughly 50,000 copies.

years.h: Jawbox's Savory hits MTV, Conan and Beavis and Butt-Head
years.p: The Savory single goes into rotation on MTV's 120 Minutes, gets played in-studio there and on Late Night with Conan O'Brien, and turns up on Beavis and Butt-Head. The next single, Cooling Card, barely registers.
In 1994, a year after leaving Dischord, Jawbox are the support act on a Stone Temple Pilots tour.

years.h: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, August 19, 1994
yt: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, August 19, 1994

eras.title: Their best record, and a label that folded under it
eras.text: Jawbox made Jawbox, the album J. Robbins still calls their best, then watched TAG, the Atlantic imprint releasing it, disappear. By 1997 drummer Zach Barocas was headed for film school and the band was done.

years.h: Jawbox split a live LP with [[Leatherface|25d9ce8e-72f7-4250-b992-f1fb8f29917f]]
years.p: Jawbox and Leatherface share a live LP in Germany's Your Choice Live Series. Jawbox also record sessions for John Peel.
Jawbox are the first band on at the HFStival, the big D.C. radio festival, taking the day's earliest slot as the hometown band.

years.h: Jawbox, the band's third album · TAG / Atlantic / DeSoto
years.p: Produced by [[John Agnello|c7d979e9-3b10-43db-973b-7da55a8a33c7]] and released on TAG, a new Atlantic imprint that folds soon after. J. Robbins still calls it Jawbox's best record.
years.xp:
A cover of [[Tori Amos|c0b2500e-0cef-4130-869d-732b23ed9df5]]' Cornflake Girl hides at the end. Wikipedia puts sales of Jawbox at around 40,000, and Robbins said the record fizzled along with the label. Desert Sea, Robbins' favorite on the album, came out of a jam. Mirrorful was the single.

TAG folded not long after the album came out. In early 1997 Jawbox and Atlantic agreed to part ways.

years.h: Zach Barocas leaves Jawbox for film school
years.p: Drummer Zach Barocas heads to Hunter College in New York. [[Peter Moffett|09d1a7e7-51fd-4b48-b99b-5b6bcbc8865b]], ex-[[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]], steps in, but Jawbox's planned European tour is scrapped.
years.xp:
It wasn't the first time Barocas had walked. He had already quit once and applied to the University of Maryland, and said the Atlantic deal was what kept Jawbox going. This time he went to Hunter College in New York to study film.

[[Peter Moffett|09d1a7e7-51fd-4b48-b99b-5b6bcbc8865b]], who had drummed in [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]] and Wool, took over, but the European dates were cancelled and Jawbox broke up later that year. Moffett stayed with J. Robbins and Bill Barbot in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.p: With the Atlantic deal over and Peter Moffett replacing Zach Barocas on drums, Jawbox formally break up in 1997.

years.h: Kim Coletta and Bill Barbot marry
years.p: With Jawbox finished, bassist Kim Coletta and guitarist Bill Barbot get married, Wikipedia reports.
years.xp: Coletta and Barbot had a son in 2001. According to Wikipedia, they divorced shortly after 2009. Both were back on stage together for Jawbox's 2019 reunion, and Coletta kept running DeSoto.

eras.title: Scrapbooks and airplanes
eras.text: Jawbox's odds and ends got collected on My Scrapbook of Fatal Accidents, and J. Robbins and Bill Barbot went straight into Burning Airlines with Jawbox's last drummer, Peter Moffett. Robbins was also becoming one of the busiest producers in post-hardcore.

years.p: Jawbox's B-sides, outtakes, Peel Sessions, live tracks and covers, gathered on Kim Coletta's DeSoto label.
J. Robbins, Bill Barbot and Peter Moffett's post-Jawbox band starts releasing records on DeSoto.
years.xp: Robbins' producer credits pile up in these years: [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]], [[Shiner|85e4c862-bafe-48a2-a7af-b87cc3d8a7f3]], later [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and [[Clutch|0cdb0359-5698-487d-9aae-a25fb4dcdc4d]].

years.p: Burning Airlines, the post-Jawbox band of J. Robbins, Bill Barbot and Peter Moffett, split after the aftermath of September 11 derails their touring.

eras.title: One song on network TV
eras.text: Twelve years after the split, For Your Own Special Sweetheart came back into print on the band's own terms, and Jawbox played exactly one TV spot to celebrate it.

years.h: For Your Own Special Sweetheart back in print
years.p: DeSoto and Dischord team up to reissue Jawbox's Atlantic debut, remastered by [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] on CD and LP with new artwork.

years.cap: Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, December 8, 2009
years.h: Jawbox reunite for one night on Late Night
years.p: Jawbox play Savory on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, their first performance since 1997. It's billed as a one-off.
years.xp:
The occasion was the DeSoto and Dischord reissue of For Your Own Special Sweetheart, back in print for the first time in years. Savory went out on the broadcast; 68 and FF=66 were posted online.

It was a one-off. The next Jawbox show was almost ten years away.

eras.title: Back on the road, then done again
eras.text: This time it was a real reunion: tours, a live album, even new recordings. It ran six years, swapped Bill Barbot for Brooks Harlan on guitar, and ended with J. Robbins confirming in a newsletter that Jawbox was done.

years.h: Jawbox's first tour in more than twenty years
years.p: Jawbox announce a 12-date summer tour with J. Robbins, Kim Coletta, Bill Barbot and Zach Barocas. Their Chicago show at the Metro becomes Live at Metro Chicago 2019 on Arctic Rodeo.

Jawbox announce that guitarist Bill Barbot is leaving, citing the long commute from his new home in Vermont. Brooks Harlan, guitarist in [[War on Women|69c05e9a-883b-4570-9c3d-c4bfc896a488]] and a longtime J. Robbins collaborator, replaces him.
Jawbox self-release the EP first, then Arctic Rodeo puts it out, the same label behind Live at Metro Chicago 2019.

years.h: J. Robbins confirms Jawbox is done; Las Vegas was the last show
years.p: Jawbox's October 12, 2024 set at Best Friends Forever in Las Vegas turned out to be their last. In April 2025 J. Robbins told Kyle Ryan's Band Name Bureau newsletter the band is done for the foreseeable future.
